mint.method: Frame-timed, screen-aware scripted boot using nes_core.NESEnvironment directly, rendering + visually inspecting env.get_frame() at every decision point instead of trusting RAM-diff timing alone (the wave-4 gap). NOOP x2400 to clear Konami logo/castle-art/title-card and reach the onset of the opening story-text crawl, then a START pulse-mash (10-on/20-off cadence). A direct A-mash-vs-START-mash fork test (900 frames each from the same mid-crawl snapshot) proved A does almost nothing (2 RAM bytes vs NOOP) while START skips the crawl outright into live Stage-1 gameplay (738 bytes vs NOOP, and the rendered frame shows the HUD + player sprite, not text). Once in gameplay, START doubles as PAUSE, so a further pulse-by-pulse sweep (each pulse independently probed with a fresh 120-frame RIGHT/LEFT/NOOP divergence check from that exact point) found the sequence alternates live/paused on every subsequent press; pulse 21 (frame 3030) lands UNPAUSED.
mint.liveness_probe: save candidate state; reload into a fresh NESEnvironment; hold RIGHT/LEFT/NOOP/A for 120 frames each; diff full 2KB RAM
mint.growth_check: right20_vs_base=238 -> right120_vs_base=300: still growing, not a saturated menu cursor

visual_confirmation.note: Actually viewed (not just RAM-inferred). mint_castlevania_iii_frame.png: HUD reads 'SCORE 000000 TIME 04XX BLK 1-01', Trevor Belmont sprite standing on ruined-castle terrain, enemy sprites visible -- live Stage 1, not title/text/menu. probe_castlevania_iii_right120.png vs probe_castlevania_iii_left120.png: the RIGHT-probe frame shows the camera scrolled right and the player mid-whip-attack against newly-revealed terrain; the LEFT-probe frame shows the player still pinned near the left edge against the original terrain -- visibly different outcomes from the same starting state under different held input, not a frozen/scripted screen. skiptest_*.png: the NOOP-continued fork is still inside the black-background scrolling story-text box; the START-mash fork from the identical starting point is in colored in-level gameplay -- direct visual proof START (and only START, not A) breaks out of the crawl.

odometer_gate.note: Real, non-flat x-axis under held RIGHT with full OAM churn (agent unambiguously alive and animating every step). Flat final quarter is a pure hold-right driver hitting an obstacle with no jump/attack input, not an instrument fault -- confirms the minted state is genuinely live, independent of the mint-time RAM-divergence probe.

classification_rationale: Three independent lines of evidence agree this is genuinely live, controllable gameplay, closing the wave-4 mint_failed verdict: (1) a rendered-frame visual check at the mint candidate and at both ends of a RIGHT-vs-LEFT divergence probe shows the camera/player state diverging visibly under different held input, not a static or scripted screen; (2) a full-RAM divergence probe from the same saved state shows real, non-saturating growth under RIGHT (162-207 bytes vs LEFT/NOOP, still growing from 20 to 120 held frames); (3) the odometer gate independently confirms a real 512px x-axis with full OAM churn under held RIGHT. The 2-minute/4-worker smoke then grew the archive 1 -> 173 cells with the frontier still wide open and the room/screen counter advancing through 2 real transitions -- the SOUND_ADVANCING shape (still climbing at cutoff), not a freeze.
wave4_root_cause_confirmed: Wave 4's mint_failed verdict was a probing-technique limitation, not a real unskippable-boot property: the game DOES have a real, START-skippable opening cinematic (the classic Dracula backstory text crawl), and wave 4's periodic-START mash schedule was in fact hitting the crawl-skip trigger, but its blind full-RAM-diff heuristic misread the crawl's own high churn (text scrolling + border torch animation) as still-scripted content, AND once past the crawl its continued mashing was toggling PAUSE on alternating presses, landing its final snapshot on a paused frame (near-zero RAM divergence under any input) that looked identical to a frozen demo loop. Both effects are resolved here by (a) rendering and visually inspecting frames at every decision point instead of trusting RAM diffs alone, and (b) a pulse-by-pulse RIGHT/LEFT/NOOP divergence sweep that isolated exactly which pulse-count lands unpaused.
